purpose: Indomethacin is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by conditions like arthritis, gout, bursitis, and tendinitis. It can also help reduce fever. Doctors sometimes use it for other conditions like a heart problem in newborns called patent ductus arteriosus.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Indomethacin works by blocking the enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) that produce these chemicals. With fewer prostaglandins, you feel less pain and swelling.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or indigestion are the most common issues. You might also experience headache, dizziness, or diarrhea. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of stomach ulcers or bleeding, especially with long-term use. It may also raise your risk of heart attack or stroke, so people with heart disease should use it cautiously. Avoid alcohol while taking it. Do not use it if you are pregnant, especially in the last trimester. Tell your doctor if you have kidney, liver, or heart problems before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 25 to 50 mg taken 2 to 3 times a day with food or milk. Your doctor will start you on the lowest dose that works for you. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary depending on your condition.
